I added `from __future__ import annotations` to all 20 carrier modules in `shop/carriers/` and left `__init__.py` alone. Each file gains exactly one line and nothing else changed.

In every module the line goes directly above `import re`, so it's the first import. It sits below the `# TODO` comment and the module docstring, because Python only allows a `__future__` import to be preceded by comments, blank lines and the docstring. Putting it on line 1 would also have stopped that string from being the module's docstring.

**Tests:** all 6 pass. pytest isn't installed here, so I ran them with `python3 -m unittest discover`. None of those tests touch the carrier modules (they cover cache, orders and pricing), so I also imported `shop.carriers`, and all 20 carrier classes loaded without errors.

The changes aren't committed.
